name: pd.Series()
desc: A single column of values. Pandas adds a numbered index on the left.
code:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30])
print(s)
out:
0    10
1    20
2    30
dtype: int64

name: A chosen index
desc: The index can be any set of labels instead of 0, 1, 2.
code:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=["a", "b", "c"])
print(s)
print(s["b"])
out:
a    10
b    20
c    30
dtype: int64
20

name: pd.DataFrame()
desc: A table. Built from a dictionary, each key becomes a column name.
out:
name  dept
0  Rahul    HR
1  Priya  Tech

name: read_csv()
desc: Loads a comma-separated file into a DataFrame.
code:
import pandas as pd
open("staff.csv", "w").write("name,dept\nRahul,HR\nPriya,Tech\n")

df = pd.read_csv("staff.csv")
print(df)
out:
name  dept
0  Rahul    HR
1  Priya  Tech

name: head() and tail()
desc: The first or last rows. The default is five; pass a number for more or fewer.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.head(3))
print()
print(df.tail(2))
out:
name   dept  salary  exp
0  Rahul     HR   47764    4
1  Priya   Tech   62990    7
2   Amit  Sales   51200    3

    name  dept  salary  exp
3  Kavya  Tech   58300    6
4  Arjun    HR   45100    2

name: loc  —  by label
desc: Selects rows by their index label.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],

})

print(df.loc[0])

dept         HR
salary    47764
exp           4

    name   dept  salary  exp

name: iloc  —  by position
desc: Selects rows by their position. Unlike loc, the stop position is not included.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.iloc[0:2])
print()
print(df.iloc[-1])
out:
name  dept  salary  exp
0  Rahul    HR   47764    4
1  Priya  Tech   62990    7

name      Arjun
dept         HR
salary    45100
exp           2
Name: 4, dtype: object

name: Rows and columns together
desc: Give the rows first, then the columns.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.loc[0:2, ["name", "salary"]])
print()
print(df.iloc[0:2, 0:2])

0  Rahul   47764
1  Priya   62990
2   Amit   51200

    name  dept
0  Rahul    HR
1  Priya  Tech

name: at  —  a single cell
desc: Reads one value, given the row label and the column name.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.at[0, "name"])
print(df.at[3, "salary"])
out:
Rahul
58300

name: iat  —  a single cell by position
desc: The same as at, but both the row and the column are given as numbers.
code:

})

print(df.iat[0, 0])
print(df.iat[3, 2])
out:
Rahul
58300

name: A condition
desc: Comparing a column to a value returns True or False for every row.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df["salary"] > 50000)
out:
0    False
1     True
2     True
3     True
4    False
Name: salary, dtype: bool

name: Using the condition
desc: Putting the condition inside the brackets keeps only the rows where it was True.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df[df["salary"] > 50000])
out:
name   dept  salary  exp
1  Priya   Tech   62990    7
2   Amit  Sales   51200    3
3  Kavya   Tech   58300    6

name: Two conditions
desc: Use & for and, | for or. Each condition must be inside its own brackets.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df[(df["dept"] == "Tech") & (df["salary"] > 55000)])
print()
print(df[(df["dept"] == "HR") | (df["exp"] > 5)])
out:
name  dept  salary  exp
1  Priya  Tech   62990    7
3  Kavya  Tech   58300    6

    name  dept  salary  exp
0  Rahul    HR   47764    4
1  Priya  Tech   62990    7
3  Kavya  Tech   58300    6
4  Arjun    HR   45100    2

name: and does not work here
desc: The word and expects one True or False, not a whole column of them.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df[(df["dept"] == "Tech") and (df["salary"] > 55000)])
out: ValueError: The truth value of a Series is ambiguous. Use a.empty, a.bool(), a.item(), a.any() or a.all().

name: Counting the matches
desc: A condition can be summed, because True counts as 1.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print((df["salary"] > 50000).sum())
print(len(df[df["salary"] > 50000]))

name: sort_values()
desc: Orders the rows by a column. Smallest first unless told otherwise.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.sort_values("salary"))
out:
name   dept  salary  exp
4  Arjun     HR   45100    2
0  Rahul     HR   47764    4
2   Amit  Sales   51200    3
3  Kavya   Tech   58300    6
1  Priya   Tech   62990    7

name: ascending=False
desc: Reverses the order, largest first.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.sort_values("salary", ascending=False))
out:
name   dept  salary  exp
1  Priya   Tech   62990    7
3  Kavya   Tech   58300    6
2   Amit  Sales   51200    3
0  Rahul     HR   47764    4
4  Arjun     HR   45100    2

name: More than one column
desc: Pass a list. The second column breaks ties in the first.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.sort_values(["dept", "salary"]))
out:
name   dept  salary  exp
4  Arjun     HR   45100    2
0  Rahul     HR   47764    4
2   Amit  Sales   51200    3
3  Kavya   Tech   58300    6
1  Priya   Tech   62990    7

name: The original is unchanged
desc: Sorting returns a new table. Assign it if the order is to be kept.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

df.sort_values("salary")
print(df["salary"].tolist())

df = df.sort_values("salary")
print(df["salary"].tolist())

name: unique() and nunique()
desc: The distinct values in a column, and how many there are.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],

name: Column statistics
desc: The same summaries as NumPy, applied to one column.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df["salary"].sum())
print(round(df["salary"].mean(), 2))
print(df["salary"].min(), df["salary"].max())
print(df["salary"].median())
